response:
**Short answer**

Employer contributions to the National Pension Scheme (NPS) are **not** counted within the Rs 1,50,000 ceiling that applies to the aggregate of deductions under **Section 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1)**.  
They are allowed as a separate deduction under **Section 80CCD(2)**, subject to their own ceiling (Rs 50,000 or 10 % of salary, whichever is lower).  

---

### Legal basis (FY 2024‑25)

| Provision | What it says | Relevance |
|-----------|--------------|-----------|
| **Section 80C aggregate limit** | “The aggregate amount of deductions admissible u/s 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1) shall be further restricted to maximum limit of Rs. 1,50,000.”【C1】 | Shows that only the three mentioned heads are capped at Rs 1.5 Lakh. |
| **Section 80CCD(2) – employer NPS contribution** | “The amount eligible under this sub‑section is subject to a maximum limit of Rs. 50,000 and further condition that no claim should have been made under sub‑section (1) in respect of the same amount.”【C4】 | Provides the specific ceiling for employer NPS contributions. |
| **Validation rule for AY 2024‑25** | “Deduction u/s 80CCD(2) should not be more than 10 % of salary in case of employer category is other than Central Government or State Government.”【C6】 | Reinforces the 10 % of salary ceiling (in addition to the Rs 50,000 ceiling). |
| **Finance Act 2024 amendment** (proposed) | “Paid by the assessee as an employer … to the extent it does not exceed ten per cent of the salary of the employee … shall be allowed as a deduction …”【C7】 | Confirms the 10 % salary rule for employer contributions. |

---

### Interpretation

1. **Separate head of deduction** – Employer NPS contributions fall under **Section 80CCD(2)**, not under **Section 80C**. Therefore they are **outside** the Rs 1,50,000 ceiling that aggregates 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1)【C1】.  

2. **Maximum amount** – The deduction is capped at **Rs 50,000** per year, **provided** the employee has not already claimed the same amount under 80CCD(1) (the employee‑side contribution)【C4】.  

3. **Additional salary‑based ceiling** – For employers other than the Central or State Government, the deduction cannot exceed **10 % of the employee’s salary** in the previous year【C6】【C7】.  

4. **Result** – An employer can claim a deduction for its NPS contribution **up to the lower of Rs 50,000 or 10 % of salary**, and this amount **does not reduce** the Rs 1,50,000 limit available for the employee’s own 80C/80CCD(1) investments.

---

### Practical implication for a salaried individual (FY 2024‑25)

| Deduction head | Maximum allowed | Counts towards Rs 1,50,000 limit? |
|----------------|----------------|-----------------------------------|
| 80C (life‑insurance, PF, etc.) | Rs 1,50,000 (combined with 80CCC & 80CCD(1)) | **Yes** |
| 80CCD(1) – employee NPS contribution | Up to 10
